results.reason: Item 1 cites SA §2.2's automatic five-year Renewal Terms and the 270/240-day notice requirement. It calls this effectively a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Item 3 quotes §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates) and contrasts it with the Term Sheet's amber/beer/U.S.–Canada scope. It concludes Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text.

Item 2 notes the August 3, 2026 receipt recorded in Recital C and the September 2, 2026 deadline, 19 days before the Amendment's September 21 date. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted absent an express extension or waiver.

The response never discusses Amendment Section 2 replacing SA §11.2. It does not address the removal of the recall-cost carve-out or the narrowing of the indemnity carve-out, and does not mention recall or product-liability exposure now being capped.

Item 4 explains that new §14.4 overrides §14.3 to allow consentless assignment to Affiliates or successors. It notes there is no competitor exclusion and that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.
The memo states the SA §15.2 order (amendments, then SA, then QA) and says the Amendment controls where it conflicts with the SA.
The memo states that SA §11.1 caps liability at the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner and organized item by item. Each item gives a document and section location and a recommended fix.
The memo proposes specific language: a replacement §2.2, a narrowed §3.1, an Amendment No. 2 price provision, and a replacement §14.4 with a competitor exclusion.
The memo expressly says the objection window closed and advises against telling the client it can still object under §5.4.
The memo expressly says the Term Sheet does not govern and that it would not advise the client that the narrower scope controls.
